name: scene-model-mixed-formalism
title: Model-definition format: one scene, three cell types, three formalisms (ODE, Smoldyn particles, MaBoSS) sharing an extracellular field
claim: A declarative scene (cells + types) bound to a per-type model registry compiles to one composite in which metabolic cells run an SBML-style ODE, signalling cells run Smoldyn particles and fate cells run a MaBoSS Boolean network, all coupled to a shared extracellular field through typed membrane transport.
experiment: Run the scene_model composite (workspace/scenes/mixed_formalism_demo.yaml, 5 cells, 3 types) for 12 steps. Each step advances tissue mechanics, every cell's own adapter, membrane exchange with the field, and field diffusion.
outcomes: The flipbook (viz/scene-model-flipbook.html) colours cells by formalism over the field heatmap and draws the particle cells' molecules (qualitative; quantitative checks pending).

question: Does a declarative scene plus a per-type model registry compile to ONE composite where ODE, Smoldyn-particle and MaBoSS cells run together sharing an extracellular field?

study_card.goal: Compile a scene of typed cells to one composite mixing three sub-cellular formalisms over a shared field.
study_card.mechanism: A scene (cells + types) binds each cell by type to a ModelSpec (ODE / particle / Boolean); compile_scene builds one orchestrating process that steps every cell's own adapter and the shared FieldExtracellular each update.
study_card.why_before_next: This is the declarative model-definition format the atlas's CoupledCell work generalises — semantics (a typed scene) separated from mechanics (which solver runs each cell).
study_card.expected_result: The scene compiles to one composite where all three formalisms run and produce molecular state over a shared field — the declarative format works.
study_card.main_expert_question: Should the shared extracellular field carry live efflux/uptake across the membrane now, rather than being plumbed-but-inert this milestone?
